name: Gloson
body:
GLOSON
CR 8

A ghostly white boar with glowing red eyes and bristling spines stamps the ground as it prepares to charge.

XP 4,800
CE Large undead (incorporeal)
Init +9; Senses darkvision 60 ft., scent; Perception +12

DEFENSE

AC 17, touch 17, flat-footed 11 (+2 deflection, +5 Dex, +1 dodge, ?1 size)
hp 78 (12d8+24)
Fort +6, Ref +9, Will +11
Defensive Abilities incorporeal; Immune undead traits

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee ghostly slam +13 touch (4d6 negative energy and wasting disease), spectral spines +13 touch (2d6 negative energy and snag)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks powerful charge (spectral spines, 4d6), wasting disease

STATISTICS

Str —, Dex 21, Con —, Int 3, Wis 16, Cha 15
Base Atk +9; CMB +15; CMD 28 (32 vs. trip)
Feats Dodge, Improved Initiative, Jaguar Pounce, Mobility, Run, Skill Focus (Stealth)
Skills Perception +12, Stealth +13

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Snag (Su)

If the gloson charges a target and hits the target with its spectral spines attack, the target must succeed at a DC 18 Fortitude save or become incorporeal, grappled, and impaled on the gloson’s spines. The gloson is not grappled but can’t attack with its spectral spines. At the end of each turn that the target is impaled on the spines, it takes 4d6 slashing damage (DC 18 Fortitude halves). A creature that fails these subsequent saves becomes fatigued (a fatigued creature becomes exhausted).

The creature can attempt to break the grapple to free itself from the spines, which also returns the creature to corporeality.

Additionally, if the creature becomes corporeal through any other means, it harmlessly passes through the Glosson.

Wasting Disease (Su)

Disease—contact or injury; save Fort DC 18; onset 1d3 days; frequency 1 day; effect 1d4 Con damage, and the creature must succeed at another DC 18 Fort save or 1 point of damage becomes drain; cure 2 consecutive saves. The save DC is Charisma-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold or temperate land
Organization solitary
Treasure none

A gloson is a traveling spirit which takes the form of a razorback. It manifests in the midst of a long journey taken by a person or group of people, with a preference for lone travelers. The spirit attempts to hide from its prospective prey and catch its prey unaware when it charges. It must charge at its target to snag the target on its razor-sharp back spines, which also render its prey similarly ghostly.

While it runs with its victim, the spines cut into the creature, sawing it in half. The gloson continues to run until it kills its prey or until its prey escapes, either by detaching from the spines or resuming a corporeal state.

Some believe the gloson to be a unique spirit; at the very least, there have been no simultaneous sightings of the ghostly boar. The spirit prevents people on long journeys from completing their journeys directly by skewering them on its back and indirectly by inflicting a debilitating illness.

Scholars speculate the gloson was one such traveler killed by a boar and that returned as the boar’s ghostly visage with an intense jealousy of those who might survive extended walking expeditions. If the gloson is destroyed, one of its previous victims’ spirits transforms into a new gloson.
